chunks: 1. Al-Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, informed me from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from his father, from al-Husayn ibn al-Hasan ibn Aban, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Safwan and Fadalah ibn Ayyub, from Fudayl ibn 'Uthman, from Abu 'Ubaydah al-Hadhdha', who said:

I performed wudu (ablution) for Abu Ja'far عليه السلام at Jam', and he had urinated. So I handed him water and he performed istinja', then he took one handful and washed his face with it, and one handful with which he washed his right forearm, and one handful with which he washed his left forearm. Then he wiped his head and his feet with the remaining moisture.
2. And with this chain, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Fadalah, from Hammad ibn 'Uthman, from 'Ali ibn Abi al-Mughirah, from Maysarah, from Abu Ja'far عليه السلام, who said:
Wudu (ablution) is one by one, and he described the ankle as being on the upper part of the foot.

3. And al-Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, informed me from Abu al-Qasim Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan and others, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Mahbub, from Ibn Ribat, from Yunus ibn 'Ammar, who said:
I asked Abu 'Abdillah عليه السلام about wudu (ablution) for salat (prayer), and he said: once, once.
4. And with this chain, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from 'Abd al-Karim, who said:
I asked Abu 'Abdillah عليه السلام about wudu (ablution), and he said: the wudu (ablution) of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم was only once, once.
5. As for what al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Hammad, from Mu'awiyah ibn Wahb, who said:
I asked Abu 'Abdillah عليه السلام about wudu (ablution), and he said: two by two.
6. And what Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated from Safwan, from Abu 'Abdillah عليه السلام, who said:

Wudu (ablution) is two by two. The proper way regarding these two reports is that we understand them as referring to sunnah (prophetic tradition), because there is no disagreement among the Muslims that one is the obligation, and whatever exceeds it is sunnah (prophetic tradition). Also, we have already presented reports that indicate that and clarify it further.
7. What al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from al-Qasim ibn 'Urwah, from Ibn Bukayr, from Zurarah, from Abu 'Abdillah عليه السلام, who said:

Wudu (ablution) is two by two, so whoever adds more is not rewarded for it. And he narrated to us the wudu (ablution) of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم: he washed his face once, and his two forearms once, and wiped his head with its remaining moisture, and his feet. Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, may Allah have mercy on him, said: his narrating the wudu (ablution) of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم as once, once indicates that by his statement, “wudu (ablution) is two by two,” he intended the sunnah (prophetic tradition), because it is not permissible for the obligation to be twice while the Prophet عليه السلام does it once, once, along with the consensus of the Muslims that he shares with us in wudu (ablution) and its manner. This is also further confirmed by:

8. What Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from 'Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi 'Umayr, from 'Umar ibn Udhaynah, from Zurarah and Bukayr, that they asked Abu Ja'far عليه السلام about the wudu (ablution) of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم,

then he called for a basin, and he mentioned the hadith until he said: so we said, “May Allah set you aright, is one scoop sufficient for the face and one scoop for the forearm?” He said: “Yes, if you do it thoroughly; and two suffice for all of that.”

9. As for what Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Musa ibn Isma'il ibn Ziyad and al-'Abbas ibn al-Sindi, from Muhammad ibn Bashir, from Muhammad ibn Abi 'Umayr, from some of our companions, from Abu 'Abdillah عليه السلام, who said:

Wudu (ablution) once is an obligation, two times are not rewarded, and the third is an innovation. The proper understanding of his statement عليه السلام, “and two times are not rewarded,” is that if he believes that they are obligatory, he is not rewarded for them; but if he believes that they are sunnah (prophetic tradition), then he is rewarded for that. What indicates what we have said is what follows:

10. Al-Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, informed me of it from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from his father, from Sa'd ibn 'Abdillah, from Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from Ziyad ibn Marwan al-Qanadi, from 'Abdullah ibn Bukayr, from Abu 'Abdillah عليه السلام, who said:
Whoever is not certain that one washing in wudu (ablution) suffices him will not be rewarded for the two.
11. As for what al-Saffar narrated from Ya'qub ibn Yazid, from al-Hasan ibn 'Ali al-Washsha', from Dawud ibn Zurbi, who said:

I asked Abu 'Abdillah عليه السلام about wudu (ablution), and he said to me: perform wudu (ablution) three times, three times. He said: then he said: do you not frequent Baghdad and their military camps? I said: yes. He said: one day I was performing wudu (ablution) in the house of al-Mahdi, and some of them saw me while I was unaware of him. So he said: the one who claimed that you are so-and-so has lied, while you perform this wudu (ablution). He said: I said: for this, by Allah, he commanded me. For it is explicit regarding taqiyyah, and he only commanded him so as to protect him and out of fear for his life due to his presence in places of danger. So he commanded him to use that by which his life, his family, and his property would remain safe.

key_terms.التَّقِيَّةِ: dissimulation for protection in circumstances of fear or danger
key_terms.الْوُضُوءُ: wudu (ablution), the ritual purification before salat (prayer)
key_terms.بِدْعَةٌ: innovation; here, a third washing in wudu
key_terms.بِفَضْلَةِ النَّدَى: with the remaining moisture left on the hand after washing
key_terms.سُنَّةٌ: recommended prophetic practice beyond the obligatory minimum
key_terms.فَرْضٌ: obligatory duty in the legal sense
key_terms.مَثْنَى مَثْنَى: two by two; interpreted here as sunnah (prophetic tradition), not obligation
key_terms.مَرَّةً: once; a single washing understood here as the obligatory amount

ai.seo_question: How many times should each part be washed in wudu according to Shia hadith in al-Istibsar?
ai.summary: This passage gathers multiple hadith on the manner and number of washings in wudu (ablution), presenting reports that describe the obligatory washing as once for each limb and interpreting reports of twice as referring to sunnah (prophetic tradition). It also states that a third washing is bid'ah and explains one report commanding three washings as arising from taqiyyah in a setting of danger.
